overview: The primary component for section headers. Use it to establish visual hierarchy across pages and layouts, from major page titles down to smaller subsection labels.

whenToUse: For all page and section titles that establish document structure and in-page hierarchy (h1–h6)
When you need headings that assistive technologies can navigate between to understand page outline
do: Follow a logical heading order (h1 → h2 → h3) without skipping levels — this is required for accessibility
Use size 1 (h1) only once per page as the primary page title
Use the branded variant to anchor major branded sections; use accent for callout sub-headings that need extra visual distinction
dont: Don't choose a heading size based on how it looks — always match the size to the correct semantic level in the document hierarchy
Don't skip heading levels (e.g. h1 → h3); it breaks the accessibility tree and confuses screen reader users
Don't use a heading just to make text larger — use Display for decorative scale or Body Bold for emphasis within prose
